claim1Verbatim:
1. In an array of magnetic tunnel junction bits that includes first bits with a stuck-at-mid condition and second bits without the stuck-at-mid condition, the method comprising the steps of:
exposing the array of magnetic tunnel junction bits to a cycling temperature that is greater than a maximum specified operating temperature;
applying a cycling voltage to the array of magnetic tunnel junction bits that is less than an operating voltage that caused the stuck-at-mid condition of the first bits; and
while maintaining the the cycling temperature and the cycling voltage, cycling the array of magnetic tunnel junction bits such that the first bits with the stuck-at-mid condition are alternatingly placed in a first stable state and a second stable state.

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method in an array of magnetic tunnel junction bits that includes first bits with a stuck-at-mid condition and second bits without that condition, comprising: exposing the array to a cycling temperature greater than a maximum specified operating temperature; applying a cycling voltage that is less than an operating voltage that caused the stuck-at-mid condition of the first bits; and, while maintaining the cycling temperature and cycling voltage, cycling the array so that the first bits with the stuck-at-mid condition are alternatingly placed in a first stable state and a second stable state. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction. The printed text contains a doubled “the” in “while maintaining the the cycling temperature,” which is preserved in the verbatim transcription.
limitations: In an array of magnetic tunnel junction bits that includes first bits with a stuck-at-mid condition and second bits without the stuck-at-mid condition, a method comprising the following steps.
Exposing the array of magnetic tunnel junction bits to a cycling temperature that is greater than a maximum specified operating temperature.
Applying a cycling voltage to the array that is less than an operating voltage that caused the stuck-at-mid condition of the first bits.

While maintaining the cycling temperature and the cycling voltage, cycling the array such that the first bits with the stuck-at-mid condition are alternatingly placed in a first stable state and a second stable state.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 2 first adds a burn-in test on the array prior to cycling, performed at an elevated temperature relative to the maximum specified operating temperature and at an elevated supply voltage relative to a maximum specified supply voltage. Claims 3–7 further limit the method to cycling substantially immediately after burn-in, use of burn-in test equipment, a cycling temperature substantially the same as the elevated temperature, maintaining the second bits in a stable state, and a time period no greater than three hours. Claim 8 is a separate independent method of applying a magnetic field to eliminate a stuck-at-mid condition without causing other bits to develop that condition. Burn-in, test equipment, the three-hour limit and Claim 8’s magnetic-field method are not to be folded into Claim 1.
en.specificationBoundary: FIGS. 1–3 (and FIG. 4) are labeled conventional/prior art and illustrate MTJ structure and the stuck-at-mid problem. The specification and FIGS. 5–7 on official page 3 describe burn-in, memory conditioning and write-“0”/write-“1” cycling flows; those process details, times and voltage values are not numerical limitations of Claim 1 or measured-performance evidence.
en.unknowns: Measured conditioning success rate, cycle count, specific temperature/voltage values and effects on the second bits were not established. Current ownership, legal status, per-claim priority entitlement, complete global family and product mapping remain unverified.

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method of writing data to a toggle memory comprising: reading in parallel a plurality of cells of a first number of a toggle memory to obtain read data; receiving a plurality of write data units, wherein that first number is equal to or greater than a combined width of two write data units; deriving a plurality of toggle instructions that includes a first toggle instruction and a second toggle instruction, the deriving including comparing bits of the read data with bits of the write data units; toggling cells as needed as per the first toggle instruction; and then toggling cells as needed as per the second toggle instruction. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction. The printed phrase “a first number of a toggle memory” is preserved.
limitations: A method of writing data to a toggle memory.
Reading in parallel a plurality of cells of a first number of a toggle memory to obtain read data.
Receiving a plurality of write data units, wherein the first number is equal to or greater than a combined width of two write data units of the plurality of write data units.

Deriving a plurality of toggle instructions, wherein the plurality of toggle instructions includes a first toggle instruction and a second toggle instruction, and wherein the deriving includes comparing bits of the read data with bits of the plurality of write data units.
Toggling cells of the toggle memory as needed as per the first toggle instruction.
Toggling cells of the toggle memory as needed as per the second toggle instruction after the toggling cells of the toggle memory as needed as per the first toggle instruction.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 2 first limits the first and second toggle instructions to comparing a first or second set of read-data bits with a first or second write data unit. Claim 3 further maps those bit sets to first and second sets of cells and toggles those sets. Claim 4 depends from Claim 1 and adds a partition into first and second sets of cells. Claim 5 requires a unique address. Claims 6 and 7 add third and fourth toggle instructions and corresponding cell sets. Set-wise comparison, unique addressing and third/fourth instructions are not to be folded into Claim 1.

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a circuit with non-volatile storage comprising a first resistive element that is a first magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) and a first node coupled to it; a second resistive element that is a second MTJ and a second node coupled to it; a sense amplifier with a first input coupled to the first node, a second input coupled to the second node, and an output; a first conductor disposed to conduct a first current to set the first MTJ to a first resistive value and the second MTJ to a different second resistive value; and a second conductor disposed to conduct a second current to set the first MTJ to a third resistive value and the second MTJ to a fourth resistive value different from the third. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction.
limitations: A circuit with non-volatile storage.
A first resistive element comprised of a first magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) element, and a first node coupled to the first resistive element.
A second resistive element comprised of a second MTJ element, and a second node coupled to the second resistive element.
A sense amplifier having a first input coupled to the first node, a second input coupled to the second node, and an output.

A first conductor disposed to conduct a first current to set the first MTJ element to a first resistive value and the second MTJ element to a second resistive value different from the first resistive value.

A second conductor disposed to conduct a second current to set the first MTJ element to a third resistive value and to set the second MTJ element to a fourth resistive value different from the third resistive value.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 2 first requires the sense amplifier to provide the output responsive to a voltage difference between the first and second nodes. Claim 3 requires the first MTJ to have a magnetic-moment vector relative to the first conductor that is substantially different than that of the second MTJ. Claim 4 requires the output also to be responsive to a second current into the first node and a third current into the second node; Claim 5 then recites the sense amplifier in transistor terms. en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method of making an array of electrically erasable programmable memory cells arranged in a plurality of rows and columns, each cell of the type having first and second spaced-apart regions in a substrate with a channel therebetween, a floating gate insulated from the substrate and over a first portion of the channel, and a control gate insulated from the substrate, spaced apart from the floating gate and over a second, different portion of the channel. The method comprises providing a first insulating layer on the substrate; providing a first polysilicon layer thereon; providing a second insulating layer on the first polysilicon; patterning and selectively removing portions of the second insulating layer and the first polysilicon to form a plurality of spaced-apart floating gates arranged in the rows and columns, and a plurality of rows of a spaced-apart second insulating layer, each such row extending continuously in the row direction and positioned on the floating gates in that row; providing a plurality of rows of a spaced-apart third insulating layer, each extending continuously in the row direction and immediately laterally adjacent to the floating gates and to a corresponding second-insulating-layer row; and forming a plurality of rows of spaced-apart spacers, each extending continuously in the row direction, positioned on the first insulating layer and immediately laterally adjacent to the third-insulating-layer row; wherein a portion of each row of spacer positioned over the channel is a control gate for the corresponding memory cell. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction. This patent is a division of 09/110,115 (US6369420B1); Claim 1 is a method claim and must not be treated as the parent’s array-apparatus Claim 1.
limitations: A method of making an array of electrically erasable programmable memory cells arranged in a plurality of rows and columns, each memory cell of the type having a first and a second spaced apart regions in a substrate with a channel therebetween, a floating gate insulated from said substrate and over a first portion of said channel, and a control gate insulated from said substrate, spaced apart from said floating gate and over a second portion of said channel, different from said first portion.
Providing a first layer of insulating material on said substrate.
Providing a first layer of polysilicon on said first layer of insulating material.
Providing a second layer of insulating material on said first layer of polysilicon.

Patterning and selectively removing portions of said second layer of insulating material and said first layer of polysilicon, to form a plurality of spaced apart floating gates, arranged in said plurality of rows and columns, and a plurality of rows of spaced apart second layer of insulating material, each row of second layer of insulating material extending continuously in a row direction and positioned on said spaced apart floating gates arranged in said row direction.

Providing a plurality of rows of spaced apart third layer of insulating material, each row of third layer of insulating material extending continuously in said row direction and immediately laterally adjacent to said floating gates in said row direction and to a corresponding row of second layer of insulating material.

Forming a plurality of rows of spaced apart spacers, each row of spaced apart spacers extending continuously in said row direction and positioned on said first layer of insulating material and immediately laterally adjacent to said row of third layer of insulating material.
Wherein a portion of each row of spaced apart spacer positioned over the channel being a control gate for the corresponding memory cell.

Selective-masking and anisotropic-etch detail, sharp-edge oxidation, and the parent US6369420B1 array-apparatus Claim 1 are not to be folded into this Claim 1.

zh.summary: Claim 1 描述在具有第一導電型、且具有實質平面的實質單晶半導體基板中，形成雙向非揮發記憶胞陣列的方法：在該平面上沿第一方向形成多數間隔且實質平行的溝槽，每一溝槽具有側壁與底部；在每一溝槽底部形成第二導電型區；在每一溝槽中形成與側壁絕緣並隔開的浮閘，該浮閘具有靠近底部的第一端與遠離底部的第二端；在每一浮閘的第二端周圍形成穿隧氧化層；在該穿隧氧化層上形成字元區層，該層沿實質垂直於第一方向的第二方向延伸；沿第二方向把該字元區層切成多數條帶以形成間隔的字元線，各條帶彼此間隔且實質平行，並切斷每一溝槽中的浮閘；以及對每一第二導電型區與每一字元線形成電性連接。以下為對印刷權利項的技術導讀，不是法律上的權利範圍判定。印刷中 “non-volatile” 與 “bi-directional” 的連字號予以保留。
limitations: 一種在具有第一導電型、且具有實質平面的實質單晶半導體材料基板中，形成雙向非揮發記憶胞陣列的方法。
在該平面上沿第一方向形成多數間隔且實質平行的溝槽；每一溝槽具有側壁與底部。
在每一溝槽底部形成第二導電型區。
在每一溝槽中形成與該側壁絕緣並隔開的浮閘；該浮閘具有靠近該底部的第一端，以及遠離該底部的第二端。
在每一浮閘的第二端周圍形成穿隧氧化層。
在該穿隧氧化層上形成字元區層；該字元區層沿實質垂直於第一方向的第二方向延伸。
沿第二方向把該字元區層切成多數條帶，以形成多數間隔的字元線；各條帶彼此間隔且實質平行，並切斷每一溝槽中的浮閘。
對每一第二導電型區以及每一間隔字元線形成電性連接。
zh.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 2 才加入在平面上形成間隔保護材料條作為遮罩以形成溝槽的步驟。Claim 3 把該保護材料限定為氮化矽。Claim 4 才細化浮閘形成（沿側壁與底部沉積絕緣層與多晶矽，再非等向蝕刻）。Claim 5 才要求浮閘與溝槽底部絕緣並隔開。Claim 6 才把形成第二導電型區的步驟限定為離子植入。不可把氮化矽遮罩、離子植入、或浮閘與底部絕緣折入 Claim 1。

en.summary: Claim 1 describes a method of forming an array of bi-directional non-volatile memory cells in a substrate of a substantially single crystalline semiconductive material having a first conductivity type and a substantially planar surface, comprising: forming a plurality of spaced-apart, substantially parallel trenches in a first direction in that surface, each trench having a sidewall and a bottom; forming a region of a second conductivity type in the bottom of each trench; forming a floating gate in each trench insulated and spaced apart from the sidewall, the floating gate having a first end near the bottom and a second end furthest away from the bottom; forming a layer of tunneling oxide about the second end of each floating gate; forming a layer of word region on that tunneling oxide, extending in a second direction substantially perpendicular to the first; cutting the word-region layer into a plurality of strips in the second direction to form spaced-apart word lines, each strip spaced apart from and substantially parallel to the others, and cutting through the floating gate in each trench; and forming an electrical connection to each second-conductivity-type region and each word line. This is a technical reading of the printed claim, not a legal construction. The printed hyphens in “bi-directional” and “non-volatile” are preserved.
limitations: A method of forming an array of bi-directional non-volatile memory cells in a substrate of a substantially single crystalline semiconductive material having a first conductivity type, said substrate having a substantially planar surface.
Forming a plurality of spaced apart substantially parallel trenches in a first direction in said planar surface; each trench having a sidewall and a bottom.
Forming a region of a second conductivity type in said bottom of each trench.

Forming a floating gate in each trench insulated and spaced apart from said sidewall of said trench; said floating gate having a first end near said bottom and a second end furthest away from said bottom.
Forming a layer of tunneling oxide about said second end of each floating gate.
Forming a layer of word region on said layer of tunneling oxide; said layer of word region extending in a second direction substantially perpendicular to said first direction.

Cutting said layer of word region in a plurality of strips in said second direction to form a plurality of spaced apart word lines; each strip spaced apart from one another and substantially parallel to one another, and cutting through the floating gate in each trench.
Forming an electrical connection to each of said region of second conductivity type and each of said plurality of spaced apart word lines.
en.dependentClaimBoundary: Claim 2 first adds forming spaced-apart strips of protective material on the planar surface as a mask to form the trenches. Claim 3 limits that protective material to silicon nitride. Claim 4 first details floating-gate formation (depositing an insulating layer and polysilicon along the sidewall and bottom, then anisotropically etching). Claim 5 first requires each floating gate to be insulated and spaced apart from the bottom of the trench. Claim 6 first limits forming the second-conductivity-type region to ion implanting. A nitride mask, ion implantation, and insulation of the floating gate from the trench bottom are not to be folded into Claim 1.
en.specificationBoundary: FIGS. 1a/1b show the finished structure; FIGS. 2A-2K show process steps. Specification discussion of an oxide of 60–100 Å, a nitride of 200–300 Å, a trench depth of 300–500 Å, and particular program/erase voltages (such as ±12 V) is not a numerical limitation of Claim 1 or measured-performance evidence. The brief lists only FIG. 1A, FIG. 1B and FIGS. 2A-2K; there is no FIG. 3.
en.unknowns: Measured alignment accuracy, coupling ratio, cell area and bidirectional operating margins were not established. Current ownership, legal status, per-claim priority entitlement, complete global family and product mapping remain unverified.
